items.title: Beginner's Guide to Blockchain Real Estate Platforms
items.tldr: A plain introduction to what blockchain property platforms claim to offer - transparency, security, fewer intermediaries - pitched at someone who has never bought a token of anything.

items.title: Why 0xEquity Focuses on Single-Family Properties
items.tldr: Single-family homes cost far less to acquire than multi-family or commercial property, which is what makes a bootstrapped portfolio possible at all. The scalability argument, laid out plainly.

items.title: Maintaining Bug Zero With Our Red Team Agent
items.tldr: An internal agent that pulls context from Sentry, CloudWatch and Grafana to keep the bug count at zero. Concrete, unglamorous, and more useful than most agent write-ups.

items.title: Shared Engineering Team Wallets
items.tldr: Getting funds to engineers, on the right chain, without handing everyone the treasury key. A short account of a pattern that keeps reappearing because the obvious answers all fail.

items.title: Using Splits to Escrow an OTC Deal
items.tldr: A neutral onchain account holds buyer funds, seller assets and collateral, then settles atomically. A clean worked example of removing a trusted middleman without adding a protocol.

items.title: 3,000+ Lending Markets, Made Comparable
items.tldr: A quoted APY means little when collateral rules, oracle choice and liquidation penalties all differ. On the work of normalising thousands of markets into something rankable.

items.title: CDP Lending: Liquity V2, Forks & River
items.tldr: Collateralised debt positions keep being rebuilt with slightly different liquidation and rate mechanics. Compares Liquity V2 and its descendants on precisely those points.

items.title: Intents Are Too Narrow and Too Centralized
items.tldr: A sceptical read on intent architectures: expressive enough for swaps, awkward for much else, and reliant on a small set of solvers. Argues the design is currently oversold.

items.title: Adding Liquidity to Meteora: A Pool Creation Guide
items.tldr: Step by step through DAMM v2 pool creation and fee configuration, which is the part where a small misconfiguration quietly costs you for the life of the pool.

items.title: How to Create a Liquidity Pool for Your Solana Token
items.tldr: Compares Raydium and Meteora pool types and walks the setup. Genuinely useful because pool choice is made once and is awkward to undo afterwards.

items.title: How to Create and Deploy Your Own ERC-20 Token
items.tldr: A deployment walkthrough on a new EVM chain. Worth reading for what the standard actually requires versus what tooling adds on top.

items.title: Driving Saturn's Revolution in Bitcoin DeFi
items.tldr: An engineering account of building DeFi where the base layer offers almost no programmability. The constraints are the interesting part.

items.title: Engineering tBTC on Sui: Bitcoin's First Live Non-EVM Integration
items.tldr: Porting a Bitcoin bridge to a chain with a completely different object model. Interesting for the assumptions that turned out to be EVM-specific rather than universal.

items.title: A Practical Guide to LP Automation
items.tldr: Concentrated liquidity only earns while the price stays in range, which turns providing it into an ongoing job. Covers what automated rebalancing does and what it costs you.

items.title: Dynamic Trade Routing: Why Splitting Your Swap Gets You a Better Price
items.tldr: A single pool charges you for depth it does not have. Explains why breaking one order across several venues beats the best individual quote, and where the saving stops covering gas.

items.title: OnlyFence: DeFi Guardrails for the Age of AI Agents
items.tldr: Letting an agent transact means deciding in advance what it may never do. A concrete look at building that fence rather than trusting the model to stay inside an imaginary one.

items.title: Can AI Agents Actually Pull Off DeFi Exploits?
items.tldr: Agents are demonstrably good at spotting vulnerabilities; this benchmarks whether they can write working exploits too, using real onchain price-manipulation attacks as the test cases.

items.title: How Stablecoins Become Money: Liquidity, Sovereignty, and Credit
items.tldr: Being fast, cheap and programmable is not the same as being money. Works through the liquidity, sovereignty and credit questions a self-custodial bearer asset raises once it carries real volume.

items.title: What Is a DUNA? A Legal Entity for Decentralized Orgs
items.tldr: The corporation was the last great answer to getting people with different incentives to cooperate. Argues the DUNA is the equivalent structure for networks nobody owns, and explains what it actually is.

items.title: Broad Onchain Contraction Defined Crypto Markets in H1 2026
items.tldr: A short data note arguing the contraction was broad rather than concentrated in one sector. Useful as a counterweight to narratives built on a single chart.

items.title: Rebuilding securities finance on Aave V4
items.tldr: Repo alone averages around $12.6 trillion in daily exposures in the US, almost all of it offchain. This sets out how V4's Hub and Spoke split could carry that collateral machinery onchain.

items.title: Unlimited Lending Market Structures
items.tldr: Market structure decides who may borrow against what, and who absorbs the risk when it goes wrong. A tour of those tradeoffs, and why V4 separates shared liquidity from the markets drawing on it.

items.title: Why Chainlink CCIP Secures Aave Protocol and the Aave App
items.tldr: Aave routes GHO transfers and multi-chain governance over CCIP instead of running its own bridge. Worth reading for what that choice assumes about trusting cross-chain messaging.

items.title: Canonical Bridges vs Third-Party Bridges: What's the Difference?
items.tldr: One is the chain's own official route with its withdrawal delay; the other fronts liquidity to make it fast. They solve different jobs, and this is clear about when each is right.

items.title: Crosschain Swaps Explained: Swap and Bridge in One Transaction
items.tldr: Trading a token on one chain for a different token on another, without doing it as two steps. Walks through how the swap and the bridge get composed into a single action.

items.title: No Gas on a New Chain? How to Arrive With ETH Ready to Spend
items.tldr: Landing on a chain with assets you cannot move because you have no native token is a genuinely common trap. Explains how to arrive already able to transact.

items.title: Consent Governance at Scale: From Cookie Banners to Operational Proof
items.tldr: Collecting consent is easy; proving months later what a specific user agreed to, under which legal basis, is the hard part. Very long and built around producing audit-ready evidence.

items.title: Cookie Compliance Is an Operational Governance Problem
items.tldr: Treats the banner as the least interesting part and focuses on classifying, governing and evidencing the tracking that sits behind it.

items.title: Pseudonymization After SRB/Deloitte: Re-Identification Is an Engineering Test
items.tldr: Pseudonymised is not anonymous, and regulators increasingly treat the difference as something you must demonstrate. Long, dense, and unusually rigorous on where the line now sits.

items.title: Efficient Sorter: The Winning Solutions
items.tldr: Published solutions from a gas-optimisation contest. Reading how other people solved the same constrained problem is one of the fastest ways to improve at Solidity.

items.title: Fibonacci Neighbor: The Winning Solutions
items.tldr: Another set of contest answers, this time on an algorithmic challenge. Useful for seeing where clever maths beats clever code and where it does not.

items.title: Meet AgorApp
items.tldr: An interactive IDE for learning Web3 engineering by writing code rather than reading about it. Sets out the case for practice-first learning in a field that mostly ships documentation.

items.title: 5 New AI Apps Built on Akash
items.tldr: From simplified agent deployment to gesture-controlled glasses. Useful as evidence of what people actually build on decentralised compute rather than what it is pitched for.

items.title: AI's Infrastructure Problem Is Bigger Than the Grid
items.tldr: Close to half of US data centres planned for 2026 are expected to slip or be cancelled. Digs into causes that go well beyond power availability.

items.title: Cloud Sovereignty Should Include Architecture
items.tldr: Europe's sovereignty debate skips the layer that decides who can switch a system off, who can read what is inside it, and whether anyone outside the provider can verify either answer.

items.title: Decentralized Cloud Gaming: How It Works
items.tldr: Games are the hardest test of decentralised compute because latency is unforgiving. Covers distributed GPU rendering and where the model genuinely stops working.

items.title: Unlocking Confidential Decentralized Computation with GPUs
items.tldr: Confidential computing on CPUs is well trodden; doing it on GPUs is considerably less so. On what accelerated confidential workloads require and what they still leak.

items.title: How Algebra Made QuickSwap Liquidity 4x More Fee-Efficient
items.tldr: A case study with actual numbers: QuickSwap's Algebra-based V3 earned 4.1x the fees and 17x the volume per dollar of TVL compared with its own V2 on Polygon.

items.title: How Algebra's NAV Plugin Enables Efficient RWA Trading on Base
items.tldr: Tokenized real-world assets price off net asset value rather than order flow, which breaks the usual AMM curve. Covers how an oracle-aware plugin reshapes the pool around that.

items.title: Clearing and Settlement for Tokenized Securities
items.tldr: Measures onchain settlement against DTCC and T+1, and is refreshingly blunt about the netting and fail-handling that traditional clearing does quietly and crypto has no equivalent for.

items.title: Qualified Custodian for Tokenized Securities Explained
items.tldr: Holding a tokenized security is not the same job as holding a token. Sets out what the qualified-custodian standard actually demands, and which parts of it nobody can yet answer onchain.

items.title: Tokenized Equities: How Onchain Stocks Work
items.tldr: What a tokenized share actually represents, who holds the underlying stock, and where faster settlement changes the economics rather than just the wrapper around them.

items.title: Decentralized Identity in the Automotive Industry
items.tldr: Identity for machines and parts rather than people, worked through with a standards body and a real supply chain. A grounded counterweight to abstract DID discussion.

items.title: Decentralized Identity in Web3: Control Your Data and ID
items.tldr: Verifiable credentials let you prove a claim without the issuer being asked each time. A solid primer on how that differs from logging in with a provider.

items.title: Security Risks of Using Cross-Chain Bridges
items.tldr: Works through why bridges keep getting drained, using real breaches rather than abstractions. The recurring theme is trusted validator sets rather than clever cryptography failing.

items.title: What Is Cross-Chain and Multichain?
items.tldr: The two terms get used interchangeably and mean quite different things: one moves value between chains, the other simply deploys in several places. Clears that up early.

items.title: What Is Gas Refueling in Crypto?
items.tldr: Arriving on a new chain holding tokens you cannot move is a genuinely common dead end. Explains the refuelling pattern that avoids it and where it can still fail.

items.title: EVM Mirror: Mind the Gap Between Audit and Deployment
items.tldr: The code that was audited and the bytecode that ended up onchain are not always the same thing. On closing that gap, which is a quietly common source of risk.

items.title: Verifiable Secret Ballots With Interfold and Aragon
items.tldr: Onchain voting is transparent by default, which is exactly wrong for a secret ballot. Describes a CRISP-based implementation that keeps votes private while still verifiable.

items.title: Binance Arbitrage: Fee Optimization, API Limits and Strategies
items.tldr: The longest of the set, and the most practical: fee tiers, API rate limits, and triangular routes. Rate limits are what actually kill these strategies at scale.

items.title: Money Flow Index: A Complete Guide for Crypto Trading
items.tldr: A volume-weighted momentum indicator, explained properly rather than as a signal to copy. Covers divergence and where the reading misleads.

items.title: Binance-Bybit BTC Arbitrage: Strategy, Fees and Execution
items.tldr: Works a single pair between two venues in detail: identifying 0.3-0.5% spreads, then showing how taker fees decide whether the trade was ever profitable.

items.title: Cryptocurrency Coins vs Tokens: What's the Difference?
items.tldr: A coin has its own chain, a token borrows someone else's. The distinction sounds pedantic until it determines who can freeze your balance.

items.title: How Six Venues Priced the SpaceX IPO Before Nasdaq Did
items.tldr: $3.23B of SPCX traded across six venues before SpaceX listed, and every one of them priced above the open - Ventuals closest at +15.3%, trade.xyz widest at +18.2%. Tracked tick by tick.

items.title: Who Is Buying RWAs? Tracing 71,697 Buyers and $91.3B Onchain
items.tldr: Rather than estimating demand for real-world assets, this counts it: 71,697 distinct buyers and $91.3B traced onchain, with the concentration laid out plainly.

items.title: Why Hyperliquid Lags Binance: Perp DEX Lead-Lag Analysis
items.tldr: Price discovery still begins on centralised venues and arrives onchain a beat later. Measures that lag directly, which matters if you assume a perp DEX prints the true price.

items.title: Blockchain and Parametric Insurance
items.tldr: Parametric policies pay out on a measured trigger rather than an assessed claim, which is exactly the shape a smart contract handles well. A good fit worth understanding.

items.title: Blockchain and the EU Digital Battery Passport
items.tldr: A regulated traceability requirement with real deadlines, which makes it one of the few enterprise blockchain cases driven by law rather than by interest.

items.title: Securing Solidity Smart Contracts: Essential Audit Insights
items.tldr: The longest piece here, covering common vulnerability classes, how to fix them, and where AI-driven tooling genuinely helps versus where it produces noise.

items.title: 3 Different Ways of Filing Your Crypto Taxes
items.tldr: Lays out the realistic options, from doing it yourself through software to handing everything to an accountant, with what each actually demands of your records.

items.title: Atomic Wallet Security
items.tldr: How the wallet handles keys, backups and recovery. Worth reading critically given the platform's own history, and useful as a checklist of what to ask any wallet.

items.title: A Vault-First Roadmap: Catalysing Bitcoin DeFi
items.tldr: Babylon has activated 90k+ BTC with 57k+ currently staked, numbers comparable to Coinbase's cbBTC. Argues holders keep choosing trustless staking over bridging, and that vaults are the way forward.

items.title: Babylon: A Game-Changing Approach to Scaling Bitcoin
items.tldr: Rather than stacking new layers on Bitcoin, Babylon extracts security from the Bitcoin chain and shares it with proof-of-stake networks like Cosmos, BNB Chain, Polkadot and Polygon.

items.title: Balancer V3 Review: Custom Pools and Hooks
items.tldr: Balancer's weighted and custom pools behave quite differently from a standard constant-product AMM. Goes into the hooks, the fee mechanics and the security surface they add.

items.title: Curve Finance Review: Still Best for Stablecoin Swaps?
items.tldr: Curve's invariant is built for assets that should trade near parity, which is why it wins on stables and loses elsewhere. Revisits whether that advantage still holds.

items.title: Raydium vs Orca: Solana DEX Rates Compared
items.tldr: Two Solana venues with different pool designs, compared on realised execution rather than headline fees. The gap between the two numbers is the interesting part.

items.title: Multiproofs on Base
items.tldr: Fast withdrawals require confidence that the proof system itself is not wrong. Running multiple independent proofs is how Base hedges that, and a step toward Stage 2 decentralisation.

items.title: Native Account Abstraction
items.tldr: EIP-8130 moves account abstraction from a bolted-on layer into the protocol itself. Covers where the gas savings actually come from once the bundler is no longer in the way.

items.title: Postmortem: June 25th Block Production Outage
items.tldr: A public, detailed account of why block production stopped and what was changed afterwards. Postmortems like this teach more about L2 architecture than any launch announcement.

items.title: How Liquid Staking Helps Manage Risks in Crypto Investments
items.tldr: Capital size tends to dictate strategy: small books chase growth, large ones want yield without lockup. Positions liquid staking against that split rather than as a universal answer.

items.title: How Liquid Staking Impacts Capital Efficiency
items.tldr: Ordinary staking locks capital; liquid staking hands you a claim you can reuse elsewhere. Follows what that reuse does to your risk once the receipt token is leveraged.

items.title: Intro to Liquidity Pools: Structure, Risks, and Rewards
items.tldr: Starts from what a pool actually is at the contract level before touching returns, which is the right order. Impermanent loss is explained rather than mentioned in passing.

items.title: Deploy a Private IBFT 2.0 Network
items.tldr: Deploys a whole IBFT 2.0 network - bootnode, RPC node, three nodes, a block explorer, plus Prometheus and Grafana - onto one Azure VM in minutes. The fastest route to a chain you fully control.

items.title: Deploy a Smart Contract on a Private Network
items.tldr: Deploying a contract with eth_sendSignedTransaction and web3js, signing and serialising the transaction yourself rather than letting a framework hide the step.

items.title: Detect Privately Built Transactions
items.tldr: An end-to-end plugin tutorial for flagging transactions that never appeared in the public mempool, which is a practical way into how private orderflow actually reaches a block.

items.title: When Yield Optimization Got Smart: Rosetta and $270M in Self-Orchestrating Strategies
items.tldr: Moving capital between yield sources normally means a keeper bot and a lot of trust. A technical account of pushing that orchestration into the transaction itself.

items.title: Sign the Outcome, Not the Steps: Why Batch Transactions Need Post-Conditions
items.tldr: Approving a sequence of calls is not the same as approving what they add up to. Argues for signing the end state, so a batch cannot quietly reroute value along the way.

items.title: Weiroll vs Smart Batching: A Deeper Comparison
items.tldr: Two designs for chaining calls together, differing on where intermediate results live and who can inspect them. Specific enough that you could actually pick one.

items.title: Cross-chain and Predicate-Based Simulations with ERC-8211
items.tldr: Simulating a transaction spanning several chains means predicting state you cannot yet read. Covers predicate-based simulation and the failures it is meant to surface early.

items.title: Rails and Cargo: Why EIP-8141 Is the Transport That Ships ERC-8211
items.tldr: A standard is inert without a way to deliver it to real users. Separates the batching format from the transport carrying it, and makes the case that transport was the harder half.

items.title: One Address, One Invoice: Multi-Chain Reconciliation on ERC-8211
items.tldr: Accepting payment across several chains usually produces several addresses and a reconciliation mess. Describes collapsing that back to a single identity per invoice.

items.title: Smart Batching SDK: Building on ERC-8211 Without Touching Solidity
items.tldr: Batched conditional transactions have historically meant deploying a contract. Walks through composing the same behaviour from the client instead, with the tradeoffs stated openly.

items.title: Liquidity Pools: What They Are and How They Work
items.tldr: Starts from the pool itself, then automated market makers, the pool types that exist and what providing liquidity commits you to. Thorough for a beginner piece.

items.title: 3 Tax and Accounting Implications of the Wormhole Hack
items.tldr: 120,000 ETH, around $323M, left through the Wormhole bridge in what was then the second-largest DeFi exploit. Uses that to work through how a loss of this shape lands on the books.

items.title: 6 Things to Know About Accounting for NFTs
items.tldr: NFT sales topped $44 billion in a year and a single Beeple collage sold for $69 million, none of which existing accounting standards anticipated. Six practices for handling the gap.

items.title: The Inconvenient Truth About Blockchain Integrations
items.tldr: Vendor-framed and openly so, but candid that 'blockchain integration' too often means hoping your API calls hold - and that public data is not the same as usable data.

items.title: Blockaid's Response to the CFTC on Prediction Markets
items.tldr: A submitted comment letter on the CFTC's proposed public interest framework. Reading a real regulatory filing teaches more about the constraints than any summary of one.

items.title: Onchain Monitoring for Trading Firms: Real-Time Risk Visibility
items.tldr: A desk needs to know not just what it holds but everything those positions quietly depend on. On making that second layer visible while capital is still deployed.

items.title: Prop Desk to Curator: JPEG Trading's Security Evolution
items.tldr: A fast-moving book across 100+ protocols and 15+ chains, and what had to change operationally to keep it safe. Concrete case study rather than a capability list.

items.title: Cross-Border Payments Visibility: From Fragmented Data to Insight
items.tldr: A payment crossing three systems produces three partial records and no single truth. On assembling those into something a finance team can actually reconcile against.

items.title: Stablecoin Onboarding for Enterprises
items.tldr: The blocker for enterprise stablecoin adoption is rarely the technology; it is approvals, compliance sign-off and reconciliation. Practical about sequencing those.

items.title: Wallet Security Automation: Keeping Digital Currencies Safe and Compliant
items.tldr: Manual approval processes do not survive contact with volume. On automating the controls without quietly removing the oversight they were meant to provide.

items.title: Calidus Pool Keys: Secure SPO Interaction on Cardano
items.tldr: Stake pool operators previously had to touch cold keys to prove who they were. Explains the delegated key scheme that removes that, and why it matters operationally.

items.title: IceBreaker Spotlight: Building Lace Pool
items.tldr: A stake pool operator's account of moving from design work into running infrastructure. Worth reading for the unglamorous reality of node operation.

items.title: IceBreakers: How SPOs Earn Revenue by Decentralizing an API
items.tldr: API infrastructure is a genuine centralisation point that rarely gets discussed. On paying independent operators to run it, and whether the incentives actually hold.

items.title: Adding a ZetaChain-EVM RPC Endpoint to MetaMask
items.tldr: A short walkthrough for pointing a wallet at a specific RPC provider. Doing this once makes clear how much your wallet depends on whoever answers those calls.

items.title: 5 Smart Reasons to Track Your Crypto Transactions Today
items.tldr: The case for recording transactions as they happen instead of reconstructing years of history under a deadline, aimed at people assuming their exchange kept the records.

items.title: Bank Frozen Your Crypto? How to Provide Proof of Funds
items.tldr: What to assemble when a bank freezes a crypto-linked deposit and asks where the money came from. Proof of funds turns out to be a documentary problem rather than a legal one.

items.title: Building an AI Agent From Scratch
items.tldr: A minimal assistant written in TypeScript, used to strip agents down to their actual moving parts. Far more instructive than reading about frameworks.

items.title: Evaluating Agent Skills: Testing Whether They Are Actually Useful
items.tldr: 92 A/B evaluations run to measure whether agent skills genuinely improved capability. Rare in publishing a measurement rather than an impression.

items.title: RAG From the Ground Up
items.tldr: Builds retrieval-augmented generation from nothing: ingestion, retrieval, generation, and crucially how they evaluated whether it worked. The evaluation half is what most write-ups skip.

items.title: What Is Bundling in Crypto?
items.tldr: Grouping several transactions into one atomic execution so they either all land in order or none do. Explains why ordering guarantees matter far more than the gas saving.

items.title: Send Money Home Cheaper and Faster With Stablecoins
items.tldr: Traditional remittance takes an average 6.49% per transfer and several days. Compares that against a stablecoin route without pretending the last mile is solved.

items.title: What Is a Real-World Asset (RWA)? A Guide to RWAs on Base
items.tldr: Begins at the plainest definition, a Treasury bond or a bar of gold sitting off the chain, then builds up to how those get represented on Base and where you keep them safely.

items.title: Who Is Satoshi Nakamoto? The Suspects and the Hunt to Unmask Bitcoin's Creator
items.tldr: Seventeen years after the genesis block nobody has proved who Satoshi is. Goes through each named suspect and what the evidence really amounts to, which is usually less than reported.

items.title: A Step-by-Step Guide to Ceramic's Private Data Proof-of-Concept
items.tldr: Adding privacy to a network built around open, shared data is genuinely awkward. Walks through a deliberately minimal proof of concept rather than promising a finished feature.

items.title: How Pairwise Synchronization Improves Decentralized Data Management
items.tldr: The team replaced the algorithm at the heart of the database, moving from multicast to pairwise sync. Explains what was wrong with the old approach and what the swap cost them.

items.title: OrbisDB Is a Practical Upgrade for Databases on Ceramic
items.tldr: What changes when you put a familiar database interface over a decentralised data network, and which of the usual guarantees survive that translation.

items.title: How to Run a Token Sale on Your Own Website
items.tldr: Hosting the sale yourself means owning the compliance, the contract and the failure modes that a launchpad would otherwise absorb. Practical about all three.

items.title: How to Ship a Token Launch That Runs as One Stack
items.tldr: Launches usually get assembled from four vendors that do not talk to each other. Argues for treating sale, vesting, staking and distribution as one system.

items.title: How to Ship Token Staking at TGE
items.tldr: Staking live on day one changes the circulating supply maths immediately. Covers what has to be ready before generation rather than bolted on weeks later.

items.title: A Guide to Attestations in Web3
items.tldr: An attestation is a digitally signed statement about something. Compares them directly against NFTs and POAPs to argue they may prove more useful and more scalable for identity.

items.title: How to Use Quorum Dev Quickstart With a Blockchain Explorer
items.tldr: Chainlens is now wired into the Quorum dev quickstart repo, so spinning up a private network gives you a working block explorer with it. Useful for actually seeing what your chain does.

items.title: Asset Tokenization: Digital Assets Explained
items.tldr: Defines tokenisation as representing ownership rights to real assets onchain, then covers what that buys - permissionless liquidity, open access, onchain transparency - and why it all rests on trustworthy offchain data.

items.title: What Is an Oracle in Blockchain?
items.tldr: Blockchains cannot natively reach outside data or systems. Sets out what oracles supply: connectivity plus verifiable computation for privacy, compliance and orchestration.

items.title: What is Cross-Chain?
items.tldr: The dApp ecosystem now spans hundreds of chains, L2s and appchains, none of which can natively talk to each other or to existing web infrastructure. A clean statement of the problem itself.

items.title: From "Sandboxed" Evals to Production Exploits
items.tldr: A test environment that quietly reaches real infrastructure stops being a test. Uses a Hugging Face case to show how the line between evaluation and exploitation gets crossed.

items.title: The Rise of Spot Markets for Inference
items.tldr: Long first part on where inference marketplaces actually stand, the structural inefficiencies holding them back, and the pressures that may force them to change.

items.title: When Cyber Agents Go Off-Script
items.tldr: Giving an agent internet access and relying on the prompt to contain it is not a security boundary. Argues that combination reliably produces misconduct rather than occasionally.

items.title: How Fake Staking Sites Work, and How to Spot One
items.tldr: A counterfeit Flare staking site took $8.5M in eight days. Pulls apart the two mechanics such sites rely on, plus the checks that catch them before you sign anything.

items.title: What a Smart Contract Audit Does and Doesn't Cover
items.tldr: An audit certifies one commit, not a living protocol. Roughly 75% of the value drained from Web3 came from outside any audit's scope, and that gap is the subject here.

items.title: What to Do When a DeFi Protocol Shuts Down
items.tldr: More than 40 protocols wound down in early 2026. Withdrawal order turns out to matter, and the token approvals left dangling afterwards are what almost everyone forgets to revoke.

items.title: Should You Split Funds Across Multiple Crypto Wallets?
items.tldr: Chainalysis counted 158,000 compromised personal wallets in 2025. Splitting balances across two or three wallets is less about paranoia than about capping what one bad signature can reach.

items.title: Stop Loss vs Stop Limit: Which Order Actually Protects You
items.tldr: One order type guarantees you get out, the other guarantees your price, and in a fast drop you cannot have both. Clarifies which failure you are choosing when you pick one.

items.title: 93% of Funded Prop Traders Never See a Payout
items.tldr: A report on why funded-trader programmes so rarely pay out, and how much of that is drawdown rules rather than trading skill. Worth reading before paying an evaluation fee.

items.title: An Early Look Into Binance's TradFi Stack
items.tldr: Tokenised equities trading around the clock creates arbitrage against a market that closes at four. A look at what 24/7 access actually changes structurally.

items.title: Why Are Crypto Exchanges Pushing Into Stocks, Forex, and Commodities?
items.tldr: Exchanges expanding into traditional assets is usually explained as ambition; the more convincing answer is fee structure. Covers the four categories and the economics behind each.

items.title: Crypto Accounting: Beginner's Guide
items.tldr: The hard part is not the arithmetic. Your transactions sit across several exchanges, wallets and chains with no broker assembling a statement for you, unlike buying stock through Fidelity.

items.title: Is Crypto Staking Worth It? Rewards, Risks & Taxes
items.tldr: Locking coins to secure a proof-of-stake chain pays a yield whether you run a validator or delegate to one. Covers the mechanics first, then what the rewards do to your tax position.

items.title: Prediction Markets Tax: Kalshi & Polymarket Guide
items.tldr: The income is definitely reportable; what remains genuinely unsettled is the category, because the IRS has never published a formal ruling on prediction market contracts.

items.title: "Insufficient Funds" in Your Wallet? Here's What's Actually Wrong
items.tldr: The error almost never means what it says. Six causes, nearly all of them about gas rather than balance, explained clearly enough to fix rather than guess at.

items.title: How to Choose a Wallet-as-a-Service Provider
items.tldr: A seven-step checklist covering key control, MPC security, approval flows and compliance. The key control question is the one that determines everything else.

items.title: Wallet-as-a-Service: What the Comparisons Skip
items.tldr: Most vendor comparisons weigh speed and cost. Argues the custody model is the variable that actually matters and the one nobody puts in the table.

items.title: Ten Projects Built on The Graph at ETHGlobal Lisbon
items.tldr: The interesting result is not who won but how many independent teams reached for the same data primitives. A read on what indexing gets used for in practice.

items.title: The Graph Technical Roadmap
items.tldr: Sets out multi-service blockchain data infrastructure on Horizon, a protocol intended to serve more than subgraph queries. Useful for seeing where indexing is heading.

items.title: Making Family Simpler and Safer
items.tldr: The follow-up covering what actually changed in onboarding. Worth reading alongside the first piece to see the argument turned into product decisions.

items.title: The Crypto Wallet Problem: Why We Created Family Accounts
items.tldr: Seed phrases put irreversible loss one mistake away, which no other consumer product does. A well-argued piece on why that model was never going to reach ordinary users.

items.title: The Ultimate Guide to Crypto Taxes in India
items.tldr: Roughly Rs 180 crore (~$21M) was collected as TDS on Indian crypto transactions in a single year, and most users still cannot say when it applies. Covers trading, staking, NFTs and airdrops.

items.title: Why You Should Avoid P2P Trades, and What to Do If Your Bank Account Gets Blocked
items.tldr: P2P off-ramping can leave tainted funds in your account through no fault of your own, and banks freeze first. Practical on avoiding it and on recovering if it happens.

items.title: Agent Wallets Compared: Crossmint, Privy, Turnkey, Coinbase
items.tldr: Long side-by-side of the main agent wallet providers. Vendor-authored, but detailed enough on key custody and spending limits to serve as a map of what this category has to solve.

items.title: Agentic Commerce Use Cases: 5 Examples That Work Today
items.tldr: Short and deliberately unambitious: five things agents can actually transact for right now, which is a useful corrective to the broader speculation.

items.title: What Is Account Abstraction? ERC-4337 Wallets Explained
items.tldr: A clean walk through what ERC-4337 changes about who pays gas, who signs, and what a wallet is allowed to be. Good grounding before anything agent-related makes sense.

items.title: Argentina's LIBRA Wallet Freeze: AML Screening at Scale
items.tldr: A judicial order naming 25 wallets, and what exchanges had to do about it across their books. Concrete illustration of why screening has to be programmatic rather than manual.

items.title: Uniswap v4 Permissioned Pools: On-Chain AML for Regulated DeFi
items.tldr: Compliance moving into the protocol layer changes who is responsible for screening and when it happens. Covers what that means for address checks and transaction monitoring.

items.title: x402 Payments: The Stablecoin Rail for AI Agents and APIs
items.tldr: HTTP 402 was reserved for payment and never used. Explains how a stablecoin paywall on an API endpoint finally gives it a purpose, and what an agent needs to satisfy it.

items.title: Japan's Stablecoin Moment: The New Licensing Regime
items.tldr: Starts from what a stablecoin actually does - 24-hour settlement, programmable payments, atomic delivery-versus-payment without correspondent banking - then traces how Japan chose to license it.

items.title: Stablecoins for Enterprise Treasury: MPC vs Multisig
items.tldr: Both split control, but they split it in different places, and that determines your recovery story and your audit trail. A clear-headed comparison for people who must choose.

items.title: DAO Formation: A Legal Wrapper Guide
items.tldr: How to pick a wrapper and then keep it aligned with the governance and treasury controls you actually run. The ongoing maintenance section is the part most guides omit.

items.title: DAOs and AI Agents: A New Frontier or a Risk to Decentralization?
items.tldr: Automating governance removes the human bottleneck and also removes the human check. Balanced on the legal implications, which are further from settled than the technical ones.

items.title: Incentives and Coordination in DAOs: Build an Operating System, Not a Voting Machine
items.tldr: Argues DAOs rarely fail at voting and routinely fail at coordination. Mandates and incentive design get more attention here than governance mechanics, which is the right emphasis.

items.title: Fundraising in Web3: How to Raise Capital
items.tldr: The handful of routes Web3 founders actually take to fund a company, beginning with the private raise, and the conditions under which each one makes sense.

items.title: The Most Common Challenges for Web3 Founders
items.tldr: Web3 markets and audiences are volatile and unforgiving, so founders have to read sentiment alongside building. On preparing for that rather than being blindsided by it.

items.title: The Ultimate Checklist to Launching a Crypto Token
items.tldr: A launch needs allocation models, transparent tokenomics, vesting schedules, staking infrastructure and regulatory awareness. Hype is explicitly not on the list.

items.title: The Defx Liquidity Engine
items.tldr: What sits behind a perps DEX and how liquidity gets sourced and priced. Short, but one of the few places this layer is described rather than assumed.

items.title: AWS CloudHSM Support
items.tldr: Hardware-grade key custody inside your own AWS account rather than a vendor's. Worth reading for the trust boundary it moves and the operational burden it hands back to you.

items.title: Introducing Transaction Screening
items.tldr: The first check shipped is lookalike detection for address poisoning, an attack that beats careful people because it exploits how humans compare long strings.

items.title: Introducing Vaults
items.tldr: A managed multichain account with composite balances, quarantine by default and a ledger behind it. Good on why custody needs its own data model rather than a list of keys.

items.title: DIA ZK: Verifiable Offchain Data, Proven Onchain
items.tldr: Uses zkTLS to prove a value genuinely came from a named source, with selective disclosure so the whole response need not be published. Aimed at reserves, NAV and collateral attestation.

items.title: How ST0x Uses DIA Oracles for Tokenized Equity Trading
items.tldr: Intent-based order logic on tokenised equities lives or dies on price freshness. A concrete look at what an oracle has to guarantee before that design is safe to run.

items.title: Multi-Chain Apps and the Importance of Stateless Clients
items.tldr: Every extra chain an app touches adds another RPC endpoint you have to trust. Explains how stateless clients verify data locally with proofs instead of taking a provider's word.

items.title: Pragmatic Adaptive Privacy
items.tldr: Opens by admitting privacy was never a design goal of Bitcoin or Ethereum, which is why retrofitting it is so awkward. Long and unusually honest about the tradeoffs involved.

items.title: The Code Was Fine. That's the Problem.
items.tldr: A long post-mortem on the KelpDAO exploit arguing the failure was in the trust layer, not the contracts. Makes the case that cross-chain bridges need cryptographic verification rather than multisig assurance.

items.title: Best Solana Wallets
items.tldr: A survey aimed at people arriving at Solana for the first time, weighing custody model and recovery rather than which one looks nicest.

items.title: Centralised Exchange vs Decentralised Exchange
items.tldr: Sets the two models against each other on custody, listing control and what happens when something goes wrong, rather than treating it as an ideological question.

items.title: Price Action 101: Breakers
items.tldr: Part of a trading fundamentals series. Short, focused on one pattern, and explains what the structure is supposed to signal rather than just how to draw it.

items.title: Creating Meaningful Issues: A Guide for Maintainers
items.tldr: A well-written issue does most of the work of attracting the right contributor. A practical framework that applies well beyond crypto open source.

items.title: Devcon and Devconnect Support Their Dependencies
items.tldr: Funding the libraries your event actually runs on, rather than the projects with the loudest grant applications. A small concrete example of dependency-aware funding.

items.title: Exploring Sustainable Funding for Digital Public Goods with UNICEF
items.tldr: UNICEF's innovation office piloting onchain funding for public goods is a genuine test of whether these mechanisms survive contact with institutional process.

items.title: 2026 Election Forecast Methodology Explained
items.tldr: Most forecast pages hand you a number and hide the recipe. This publishes the polling adjustments, how poll and market data get weighted against each other, and the scenario modelling.

items.title: Bitcoin Analysis: Reading the Market When It Crashes
items.tldr: A framework for reading a falling market rather than a prediction about one. Runs through the indicators and onchain signals that stay meaningful when price is moving fast.

items.title: DuelDuck for Beginners: A P2P Prediction Market Guide
items.tldr: In a peer-to-peer duel your counterparty is another user, not a house. Covers how a ticket gets priced, how Yes and No resolve, and when the USDC actually reaches you.

items.title: A Deep Dive Into TSS-MPC
items.tldr: What threshold signature schemes are, how they differ from other flavours of multi-party computation, and the security properties that follow from each choice.

items.title: Beyond the Speed Myth: TSS-MPC Performance
items.tldr: The standing objection to threshold signatures has been latency. Argues that objection is now several years out of date, and shows where the time actually goes.

items.title: Building Identity-Based Mini Apps With World ID
items.tldr: Gating an app on proof of personhood rather than on a wallet balance. A practical walkthrough of what verified human access changes about the design.

items.title: How Crypto Cards Hold Your Money: Custody Explained
items.tldr: A crypto card is really two systems stacked: payment rails and custody. Worth reading for who holds your balance between transactions, and what an issuer collapse could actually touch.

items.title: Seed Entropy: How to Verify Your Hardware Wallet
items.tldr: A seed phrase can only be as unpredictable as the randomness that produced it. Prompted by the Coldcard RNG flaw, this shows how to check where your device sources entropy.

items.title: How ENS Names Evolved
items.tldr: From a flat ownership model for .eth names through subnames and permissions to ENSv2's registry-native design. Good for understanding why the architecture ended up shaped this way.

items.title: How ENS Normalization Works
items.tldr: Two names can look identical to a person and be entirely different strings to a machine, which is precisely how spoofing works. Explains the normalization step that closes that gap.

items.title: What Makes ENS a Protocol
items.tldr: The argument that ENS is naming infrastructure and not a product: stable resolution rules, open standards, and many independent interfaces all reading the same records.

items.title: Bad Execution, Real Costs
items.tldr: Written for fintechs adding swaps without a trading desk's instincts. Makes the case that routing quality is a product decision with a measurable price, not a backend detail.

items.title: How Manipulated Quotes Create Execution, UX, and Liability Risk in DeFi
items.tldr: Some liquidity is engineered to lie: the pool quotes beautifully during routing and settles badly. On toxic pools and hooks, and who carries the loss when a router believes them.

items.title: The Next Billion Wallets Won't Know They're Using Crypto
items.tldr: Argues the next wave of wallet users never self-identify as crypto users at all, and that stablecoins plus embedded wallets are what make that possible.

items.title: Why AI Agents Need Communication Infrastructure
items.tldr: An autonomous agent still has to receive information it can trust, on time. Short piece on what that channel has to guarantee before the agent can act on anything.

items.title: Euler Primer: The Credit Layer for Programmable Finance
items.tldr: The long-form case for treating lending as modular infrastructure rather than one monolithic pool, and what that unlocks that a shared-pool design cannot.

items.title: What Is the Ethereum Vault Connector?
items.tldr: Account infrastructure built around ERC-4626 that lets vaults be used as collateral for one another. The piece of plumbing that makes modular lending composable rather than isolated.

items.title: What Is the Euler Vault Kit?
items.tldr: The framework every Euler lending vault is built from. Start here if you want to understand what is actually configurable in a lending market and what is fixed.

items.title: Lost Keys, No Lost Land
items.tldr: The obvious objection to tokenised property is what happens when someone loses their keys. Nearly six thousand words answering exactly that, which is the right length for the question.

items.title: Tether for Land
items.tldr: Takes the comparison seriously rather than as a slogan: what it would mean for land titles to move the way a stablecoin does, and which parts of property law refuse to cooperate.

items.title: Title Insurance After Tokenization
items.tldr: Short, and the most concrete evidence in the set: a tokenised property went through a conventional sale and a major underwriter wrote the title policy. Theory meeting practice.

items.title: How Does Fibrous Get You the Best Price?
items.tldr: Opens with a glossary, then traces exactly what happens between pressing swap and settlement. A good introduction to aggregation for anyone who has only used it.

items.title: Introducing FibX: DeFi Execution for AI Agents
items.tldr: Agents can reason about a trade long before they can execute one safely. On the execution layer that sits between a model's intention and an actual onchain swap.

items.title: AWS S3 Pricing: What You'll Actually Pay
items.tldr: Storage is the cheap part. Requests, retrievals and egress are where the bill comes from, and this walks each line so the total stops being a surprise.

items.title: How Browser Uploads Work With Pre-Signed S3 URLs
items.tldr: Letting a browser upload straight to storage without handing it your credentials. Covers the backend signing step and the CORS configuration that trips everyone up.

items.title: Infura IPFS Is Shutting Down: How to Migrate
items.tldr: A concrete deadline and a concrete migration path for anyone with pins on Infura. Also a useful reminder that pinned does not mean permanent.

items.title: An End-to-End Encrypted Alternative to Google Docs
items.tldr: What actually changes when collaborative editing is encrypted by default, including the features that become harder to offer once the server cannot read the document.

items.title: Google Docs and Gemini AI: The Privacy Problem
items.tldr: Your documents are not end-to-end encrypted, which means the privacy question is entirely one of trust rather than of cryptography. Direct about what that implies.

items.title: Google Docs vs Microsoft Word: Which Is Better?
items.tldr: Compares the two on collaboration, formatting and offline editing, but the privacy and security section is the part worth your time.

items.title: How Fireblocks Prevents Stuck Transactions From Freezing Ops
items.tldr: A single pending transaction can block a nonce and stall everything behind it. Short and practical on timeouts, monitoring and the replacement strategies that unstick a queue.

items.title: London Is Open for Tokenized Business
items.tldr: The UK's digital assets regime is now live, bringing FCA licensing rules and stablecoin standards with it. A readable summary of what firms actually have to do differently.

items.title: Why Enterprise AI Agents Need a Wallet Layer
items.tldr: Corporate cards assume a human approves the spend. Sets out what has to exist instead when the spender is an agent: scoped authority, revocation, and an audit trail that holds up.

items.title: An Integrated On-Chain Trigger Response Engine
items.tldr: Detecting an exploit is useless if the response takes an hour of human coordination. Describes wiring detection directly to automated action, and the risks of doing so.

items.title: Devious Transfer: Breaking Oblivious Transfer-Based Threshold ECDSA
items.tldr: Three critical vulnerabilities found in open-source threshold signature libraries. A reminder that MPC security rests on cryptographic implementations most integrators never read.

items.title: Cross Chain Swap Protocols 2026: Top 5 Compared
items.tldr: Compares five designs on the axis that matters most: who holds your asset mid-swap, and what happens if the other leg never arrives.

items.title: Native Bitcoin Swaps on Phantom
items.tldr: Bitcoin has no smart contracts to lean on, which makes non-custodial swaps genuinely hard. A short account of how that was wired into a mainstream wallet.

items.title: Fee Collector: Automatically Aggregate Protocol Fees Into USDC
items.tldr: Protocols accrue fees in dozens of tokens and then have to do something about it. A small, practical piece on turning that scatter into one denominated balance.

items.title: Introducing Gelato Turbo: High-Performance Sequencing for Rollups
items.tldr: The sequencer decides ordering and latency, which makes it the most consequential and least discussed part of a rollup. On building one for throughput without losing reliability.

items.title: Turbo Relayer: Faster Transactions, Lower Gas Overhead
items.tldr: Sub-300ms gasless confirmations by way of EIP-7702 and ERC-4337. Useful for seeing where the overhead in account abstraction actually accumulates.

items.title: Identity Infrastructure: The Binding Constraint on Democratic Funding
items.tldr: Every one-person-one-vote funding scheme decays without Sybil resistance, and allocation math has raced ahead of any ability to verify who is voting. Names the bottleneck without flinching.

items.title: Mechanism Pluralism: Why No Single Funding Model Works
items.tldr: Cross-ecosystem analysis arguing that one dominant funding mechanism is as brittle as one crop. The case for holding a portfolio of mechanisms instead of hunting for the best.

items.title: The Grantee-to-Funder Flywheel: How Early Public Goods Funding Seeds Future Funders
items.tldr: Follows specific chains of causation rather than asserting them: Plasma Group's modest QF grant to Optimism's 60M+ OP distribution, 1inch's $50K to $3M given back.

items.title: Crypto Hacks H1 2026: How the Landscape Is Changing
items.tldr: Built from 224 publicly disclosed incidents rather than impressions. Covers where the money went afterwards, which is usually the more revealing half of any hack.

items.title: Crypto Sanctions Screening: A Practical Guide for Compliance Teams
items.tldr: Screening an address is easy; screening for indirect and ownership exposure is where teams get caught out. Works through all three layers with the ordering that matters.

items.title: How to Report Crypto Scams as a Business: Country-by-Country Guide
items.tldr: Knowing you were defrauded is not the hard part; knowing who to tell, with what evidence, in which jurisdiction, is. Covers US, UK and Canadian reporting routes concretely.

items.title: Digital Asset Lineage: Tracking Where Onchain Money Came From
items.tldr: Source of funds, cost basis and partner attribution all get destroyed the moment tokens are pooled. On keeping that context attached to money as it moves.

items.title: How to Track Solana DEX Trades with the dex_swaps Dataset
items.tldr: Getting every Solana swap into your own database sounds simple until you meet the normalisation problem. A practical walkthrough of doing it in real time.

items.title: Open-sourcing Streamling: A Stream Processing Runtime for App Teams
items.tldr: A Rust stream processor built on Apache Arrow and DataFusion, with pipelines defined in YAML. Worth reading for how onchain indexing problems map onto general streaming ones.

items.title: A Step-by-Step Guide to the Bittensor Learning Track
items.tldr: Bittensor uses market mechanisms to price intelligence, split across subnets with miners and validators. This is a structured way into a design that resists casual explanation.

items.title: A Step-by-Step Guide to the Eclipse Learning Track
items.tldr: Eclipse runs the Solana VM as an Ethereum layer 2, which makes it a useful lens on what an execution environment actually is versus where settlement happens.

items.title: A Step-by-Step Guide to the Nouns Learning Track
items.tldr: One NFT auctioned every day, forever, funding a treasury the holders govern. Nouns is a strange and instructive design, and this walks through how the pieces hold together.

items.title: Dev Workshop: Building an Onramp to Any Chain
items.tldr: Seven lines of code to a working onramp. Short, and a good measure of how far the integration burden for fiat-to-crypto has actually fallen.

items.title: Halliday: The First Workflow Protocol
items.tldr: As chains and services multiplied, the hard part stopped being any single call and became sequencing them reliably. Sets out workflows as the missing abstraction.

items.title: Deploying Smart Contracts Using Hardhat Ignition
items.tldr: Declarative deployment: describe the end state and let the tool work out the ordering and resume from failures. A better model than a script that must run perfectly once.

items.title: Displaying Execution Traces
items.tldr: Short, and disproportionately useful: seeing exactly which calls ran and what they returned is the fastest way to understand why a transaction reverted.

items.title: Managing Config Values and Secrets Safely
items.tldr: Private keys in a committed config file remain one of the most common ways teams lose funds. Covers the mechanism Hardhat provides so they never sit in the repo.

items.title: The Crypto Agent Layer (Litepaper)
items.tldr: A long design document for turning stated intent into executed onchain action via a multi-agent system. Worth reading as a worked example of where such designs get hard.

items.title: Unlocking Security and Simplicity: MPC Wallets Explained
items.tldr: Multi-party computation splits a key so no single machine ever holds it whole. A readable introduction to what that buys you and what it complicates.

items.title: Breaking Down the sBTC-Wormhole Integration
items.tldr: Moving a Bitcoin-backed asset across chains means two different trust models meeting in the middle. Explains where the handoff happens and what each side assumes.

items.title: Deep Dive: How the Token Metadata API Works
items.tldr: Token metadata sounds trivial until you have to serve it consistently across standards and chains. A look at what the API actually has to reconcile.

items.title: Dissecting a Transaction Signature on Stacks
items.tldr: Pulls a signature apart field by field. Signature formats are usually treated as a black box, and understanding one properly makes a whole class of bugs legible.

items.title: LangChain and CrewAI Integration
items.tldr: Wiring live prices, DeFi analytics and token security checks into agent frameworks. Useful for seeing where an agent's data actually comes from.

items.title: MCP Integration Tutorial
items.tldr: Step by step for connecting Claude, Cursor or another MCP client to live crypto data. Practical, and a decent introduction to what MCP actually does.

items.title: REST API Tutorial
items.tldr: The plainest of the three: querying prices, yields and token security over HTTP, with no framework in the way. Start here if the others feel like too many layers.

items.title: Builder Journeys: Deploying Bridged USDC With Warp Routes
items.tldr: A team's actual path to getting bridged USDC live on their chain. Implementation detail of the kind that rarely makes it into documentation.

items.title: Builder Journeys: DIA Crosschain Oracle
items.tldr: How an oracle team delivered price data across chains, and which interoperability decisions they had to make first. Implementation detail rather than architecture diagram.

items.title: Builder Journeys: LogX Expands Trading Interchain
items.tldr: A trading venue extending across chains, told from the builder's side. Worth reading for what breaks when order flow and settlement stop sharing a chain.

items.title: Building With Modular Security Legos
items.tldr: Interoperability security is usually presented as one setting. This breaks it into composable modules you choose between, which makes the tradeoffs visible instead of implicit.

items.title: How Permissionless Is Your Interoperability Provider? A Checklist
items.tldr: A pointed set of questions to ask before depending on a bridge: who can add a chain, who can pause it, and who you need permission from. Uncomfortable for most providers.

items.title: 4 Security Testing Tools Every DeFi Developer Should Use Before Auditing
items.tldr: What to run yourself before paying anyone to audit, on the reasonable basis that auditors should not be spending their time on what a fuzzer would have caught.

items.title: 4 Wallet Security Myths That Put Users at Risk
items.tldr: Takes apart the reassuring beliefs people hold about hardware wallets and seed phrases, and is specific about what each myth actually leaves exposed.

items.title: Immunefi Arbitration: Onchain Dispute Resolution
items.tldr: Bounty disputes usually come down to severity disagreements with no neutral referee. Describes an arbitration process, which is a quietly important piece of security economics.

items.title: Top 3 Bugs from the ThunderNFT Invite-Only Program
items.tldr: Real findings from a live bounty, written up with the reasoning intact. Reading how someone else found the flaw is worth more than any list of vulnerability categories.

items.title: A Mathematical Theory of Danksharding
items.tldr: Short and unapologetically formal. If you have read the accessible explanations of data availability sampling and want the actual mathematics, this is the step up.

items.title: AMD XDNA: Meet the ZK Acceleration King
items.tldr: Proof generation is now a hardware problem as much as a cryptographic one. Benchmarks a specific accelerator architecture against the workload ZK actually creates.

items.title: Bridging the Multichain Universe With Zero Knowledge Proofs
items.tldr: Long treatment of proof-based bridging, where the receiving chain verifies mathematics rather than trusting a validator set. The most rigorous answer to the bridge problem.

items.title: DAO Taxes: The Ultimate Guide
items.tldr: Governance tokens create tax positions that nobody agreed to take on. Covers how a DAO can stay compliant when the entity itself may not legally exist anywhere.

items.title: How to Prepare for the Transition to Account-Level Cost Basis
items.tldr: New IRS rules mandate wallet-by-wallet lot tracking rather than one pooled basis. If you have been reporting the old way, this is the change that forces a rebuild.

items.title: Cardano Upgrade: The van Rossem Hard Fork
items.tldr: A hard fork is months of testing, coordination, governance debate and infrastructure work before the switch is thrown; this one enacted 18 July 2026. Strong on the process behind the headline.

items.title: Lowering minPoolCost and Increasing Smart Contract Capacity
items.tldr: One governance action bundling two changes: cutting minPoolCost to 75 ada and raising Plutus execution limits. Written so stake pool operators and DReps can vote knowing what actually moves.

items.title: Who's Standing in the 2026 Constitutional Committee Election?
items.tldr: Ten candidates for four seats, voted by DReps on a stake-weighted basis. The committee reviews governance actions for constitutional compliance, and cannot vote on their merits.

items.title: A Step-by-Step KYC Guide
items.tldr: Verification is where most people abandon a regulated platform. Useful mostly for showing exactly what gets asked for and why each item is required.

items.title: An Extensive Guide to Buying Your First Security Token
items.tldr: Security tokens carry transfer restrictions and eligibility checks that ordinary tokens do not. Walks a first purchase including the parts that will block you.

items.title: Deobfuscation Ratings, Inlining Fat Functions, and Breaking Opaque Predicates
items.tldr: Concrete techniques for undoing deliberate obfuscation. Directly relevant to anyone trying to understand what an unverified contract or binary actually does.

items.title: Mutation-Resistant Library Code Matching
items.tldr: Identifying known library code even after it has been altered to avoid detection. The cat-and-mouse framing makes the problem unusually easy to follow.

items.title: Reversing Nvidia GPU SASS Code
items.tldr: Long and deeply technical work on decompiling GPU assembly, a target with almost no tooling. Far outside the usual crypto reading and better for it.

items.title: Address Poisoning Attacks: How They Scam Web3 Users
items.tldr: The attack works because people verify the first and last few characters of an address and nothing in between. Covers detection and the habits that defeat it.

items.title: Human Behavior Causes 44% of Web3 Losses
items.tldr: Research putting nearly half of crypto theft down to human error rather than broken code, despite the billions spent on securing the code.

items.title: Solana Security: Automated Defense for Wallets and Programs
items.tldr: $250M lost on Solana in a single half-year, most of it to phishing and social engineering rather than protocol bugs. On catching those at transaction time.

items.title: How to Use Mnemonic Sharding (SLIP39): A Step-by-Step Guide
items.tldr: SLIP39 applies Shamir's Secret Sharing to split a master key into shards that need a threshold to recover, removing the single point of failure. Includes storage schemes and their risk boundaries.

items.title: Is an Air-Gapped Cold Wallet Truly Unbreakable?
items.tldr: Air-gapping removes the network as an attack surface and leaves several others intact. An unusually honest look at supply chain, firmware, and the human holding the device.

items.title: Long-Term Bitcoin Storage: Security Risks Most HODLers Ignore
items.tldr: Ten-year storage fails differently from ten-month storage: media degrades, firmware ages, heirs cannot find the instructions. Concentrates on slow risks rather than dramatic ones.

items.title: New Security Features: How to Verify a Call Is Really From Kraken Support
items.tldr: Phone scams work because there is normally no way to check who is calling. Describes an in-app verification step, and by extension why unsolicited support calls should always fail closed.

items.title: War Games: How We Built Kraken to Handle 10x the Load
items.tldr: Exchanges fail at exactly the moment everyone needs them. An engineering account of deliberately breaking your own systems to find where they give way first.

items.title: A New Automation Fee Model
items.tldr: Moving away from charging per automation run. Worth reading for how fee design shapes whether users leave automation switched on at all.

items.title: How to Use Zap In on the Krystal Wallet App
items.tldr: Entering a liquidity position from a single token instead of assembling both sides yourself. Explains the swap happening underneath and what it costs you.

items.title: Flip Orders: Concentrated Liquidity on Order Books
items.tldr: Borrows the concentrated liquidity idea from AMMs and applies it to a CLOB, aiming for AMM-style simplicity without giving up order book control.

items.title: Introducing Vaults
items.tldr: Providing liquidity to an order book without managing individual orders yourself. Short, and useful for seeing what gets abstracted away and what you still carry.

items.title: What Does a Market Maker Do?
items.tldr: The clearest of the three: what market making actually involves, and how the job differs on an AMM versus a central limit order book. Good grounding before the others.

items.title: Moving Your Funds to Lace, Carefully
items.tldr: Migrating a wallet is one of the few crypto actions that cannot be undone if it goes wrong. Orders the steps safely and is firm that you trust only official sources.

items.title: Security You Can Verify, Today
items.tldr: On inviting outside scrutiny and publishing every finding, resolved or explained - including the places where the team decided not to change something and says why.

items.title: Agentic Finance: How AI Agents Work With Lagoon Vaults
items.tldr: Moving agents from chat to actual capital means letting them discover a vault, read its state, and act on it. Describes what each of those three steps requires.

items.title: Lagoon's Fee Structure: The Four Fee Types, Explained
items.tldr: Management, performance, entry/exit and protocol fees, with the actual formulas, caps and accrual mechanics rather than a summary. Rare to see a vault show this much of its arithmetic.

items.title: More Than Vaults: Lagoon's Open Data Layer
items.tldr: An SDK reading contracts directly, plus a public GraphQL API with no key required. Worth reading for the argument that vault data should be queryable by anyone, not just the operator.

items.title: A New Era for ZK: Decentralizing the ZK Stack
items.tldr: Proof generation concentrated in a few hands recreates the trust problem proofs were meant to remove. The longest piece here, and the clearest on why prover decentralisation matters.

items.title: AI Is Scaling Faster Than We Can Verify It

items.title: The Analytics Replica Pattern for Data-Based AI
