items.title: Using a Mobile Driver's License at the Airport: How TSA mDL Acceptance Works
items.tldr: Behind one tap at a checkpoint sits a chain of trust and a pile of interoperability standards. Traces that chain, which is the clearest worked example of digital ID in production.

items.title: What Is Device Binding, and How Does It Stop a Stolen Digital ID Being Reused?
items.tldr: A digital credential that can be copied is worth very little. Device binding is the cryptographic layer that ties one to a single phone, and this explains how.

items.title: What Is Selective Disclosure, and How Do Verifiable Credentials Reveal Only What's Needed?
items.tldr: Showing a driving licence to prove your age hands over your address too. Selective disclosure turns that oversharing into proving exactly one fact and nothing more.

items.title: DeFi Wasn't Built for This
items.tldr: Research with Barter arguing that DeFi infrastructure designed around human reaction times quietly penalises autonomous agents, and what would need to change for it not to.

items.title: How SQD Validates Every Block
items.tldr: Most indexers trust whatever an RPC endpoint returns. This covers trie-rooted verification at the source instead, and why blind trust in RPC is a real correctness problem.

items.title: Votemarket Incident Disclosure
items.tldr: A second published post-mortem from the same team. Protocols that disclose properly, twice, are worth reading precisely because most disclose once and quietly.

items.title: vsdCRV Incident Disclosure
items.tldr: A compromised deployer key used to forge unbacked tokens on Arbitrum, written up with the timeline and the fix. Key compromise, not contract logic, which is the more common failure.

items.title: Diversified Staking With MetaVaults
items.tldr: Routing deposits across several underlying vaults instead of running validators directly. Explains what that spreads out and what it does not, which matters for slashing exposure.

items.title: Leveraged osETH/WETH Looping Strategy on Gearbox
items.tldr: Walks a leveraged staking loop end to end with the actual numbers attached. Useful precisely because it shows where the yield comes from and what liquidates it.

items.title: Setting Up Per-Client MetaVaults
items.tldr: How one validator fleet can serve several clients with separate staking experiences. Operationally specific in a way most staking content avoids.

items.title: Cross-chain DeFi risks: what blockchain bridge security really costs
items.tldr: Bridges exist because the best opportunities are never all on one chain, and every hop adds a trust assumption. Adds those costs up instead of waving at them.

items.title: Cross-Chain Swaps Are Not a Feature, They're the New Default
items.tldr: Bridges, atomic swaps and resolver-based HTLC each handle custody differently, and the difference decides who holds your asset mid-transfer. Read before moving anything.

items.title: DeFi Protocols Across Chains: Same Brand, Different Game?
items.tldr: A protocol on Ethereum and the same protocol on Base share a name and little else. Compares liquidity, fees and token availability across deployments.

items.title: Do Cross-Chain Bridge Users Get Better DeFi Rewards?
items.tldr: Wallet data suggesting bridge users run more deliberate strategies, set against the fees that quietly erode the difference. Data-led rather than asserted.

items.title: How to build a cross-chain DeFi strategy step by step: HTLC, RFQ, and atomic swaps
items.tldr: HTLC, RFQ and atomic swaps are not interchangeable plumbing. Each decides who carries the timing risk while value is in flight, which is the real basis for picking between them.

items.title: The future of cross-chain UX: will users even know what chain they're on?
items.tldr: Choosing a chain is still a step users perform by hand. Looks at how intents and resolvers erase that step from the interface, and what has to hold together underneath.

items.title: Regulated Perps Volume Fades in Early Phase
items.tldr: "The institutions are coming." The first full month of data says not yet: Kalshi's regulated crypto perps have not seen a day above $1.5B since 17 June, with BTC and ETH dominating what there is.

items.title: The Exchanges That Led RWA Perps' 1H 2026 Surge
items.tldr: RWA derivatives broke out in the first half of 2026, June alone reaching $467B in volume. Splits the surge by exchange and asset category rather than reporting one headline number.

items.title: Building a Strategies Platform for Cardano DeFi
items.tldr: What has to exist before automated strategies can run on a UTXO chain, where the execution model differs sharply from account-based DeFi.

items.title: Building the Hydra Transaction Stream Plugin
items.tldr: Extending Cardano's layer 2 with a plugin for streaming transactions. A concrete look at what Hydra makes possible and what it demands in return.

items.title: Introducing SuperformOS: Verifiable Strategy Engines for Programmable Vaults
items.tldr: Most 'non-custodial' vaults are still black boxes: what the vault may do, how it rebalances, how pricing updates all live offchain in private scripts. An attempt to move that logic where it can be checked.

items.title: Setting the Standard for Transparency
items.tldr: Opens by noting how many consumer apps now hold your crypto while telling you very little about where it sits. A pointed piece on what disclosure should actually mean.

items.title: Best ETH Bridge: Fees, Speed & Security Compared
items.tldr: Nine bridges lined up on cost, transfer time and, unusually for this genre, their actual exploit history. That last column is the one worth reading.

items.title: How to Bridge ETH to Arbitrum: Fees, Speed & Routes
items.tldr: The official bridge is safest and slowest; third-party routes front the liquidity and charge for it. Lays out what the seven-day wait actually buys you.

items.title: Deep Dive: Solana DApp Revenue
items.tldr: Revenue is the least flattering metric to publish and the most informative. Breaks down which applications on Solana genuinely earn and how much.

items.title: Deep Dive: Solana Developers
items.tldr: Tracks developer activity rather than price or TVL, which tends to lead the other two. Worth reading for how the measurement itself is constructed.

items.title: Deep Dive: Solana Onchain Activity
items.tldr: A monthly data read on what Solana is actually being used for, broken out rather than reported as one headline number. Long, and closer to a research note than a blog post.

items.title: Introducing ETH as Margin on Synthetix
items.tldr: The first non-stable asset accepted as collateral, which sounds simple and is not: posting a volatile asset as margin changes how liquidation has to work.

items.title: Introducing Scaled Orders on Synthetix Perps
items.tldr: Rather than one large limit at a single level, a scaled order lays a ladder across a range. Useful for understanding how execution shape changes your average fill.

items.title: Introducing TWAP Orders on Synthetix Perps
items.tldr: Time-weighted average price orders exist because pushing size through in one go moves the market against you. A clear explanation of scaling in and out over time.

items.title: ICOs Are Back: What Crypto-Native Teams Need to Know
items.tldr: After years of airdrops as the default, token launches have swung back toward sales. Sets out what has changed legally and structurally since the last time this was normal.

items.title: KYI and the Institutional Era of DeFi
items.tldr: Know Your Institution rather than Know Your Customer: what a fund needs to establish about a protocol before it can allocate, and who is positioned to attest to it.

items.title: The Complete History of Vesting: From Pension Plans to Token Lockups
items.tldr: Vesting began as a way to stop railroad workers leaving in 1875 and now governs billions in token distribution. The lineage explains several conventions nobody questions.

items.title: How to Protect Your Crypto From Phishing Scams
items.tldr: Phishing took over $1.8B in 2024, and almost none of it required breaking any cryptography. Runs through the actual vectors: cloned sites, Discord lures, malicious approvals.

items.title: Is Self-Custody Risky? Understanding Crypto Self-Custody Risks
items.tldr: Refuses the usual framing that self-custody is simply safer. Weighs the risks you take on against the ones you shed, then covers how to reduce the former.

items.title: What Is a Hot Wallet?
items.tldr: Being connected to the internet is the entire definition, and every tradeoff follows from it. A clean primer on where hot wallets fit and where they stop being appropriate.

items.title: Crypto Payroll: Paying Global Teams
items.tldr: Paying contractors across borders in stablecoins solves the transfer and creates new questions about withholding, local reporting and volatility on payday.

items.title: SPL vs Token-2022: Understanding Solana's Token Standards
items.tldr: Token-2022 adds extensions like transfer hooks and confidential balances that plain SPL cannot express. Short and clear on when the newer standard is worth the added surface.

items.title: Why Branded Token Vesting Builds Long-Term Trust
items.tldr: A vesting schedule anyone can verify onchain is a commitment; one described in a blog post is a promise. On why the difference shows up in holder behaviour.

items.title: 3 Ways to Use Fixed-Rate Loans as a Passive User
items.tldr: Written for someone who wants a known rate and no daily management. Three concrete positions, with what each assumes about where rates go next.

items.title: 3 Ways to Use Fixed-Rate Loans as an Advanced User
items.tldr: The follow-up for people who will actively manage the position: leveraging the rate view itself rather than just locking one in.

items.title: How to Avoid DeFi Liquidity Squeezes
items.tldr: Variable-rate pools like Compound and Aave can leave lenders unable to withdraw exactly when they most want to. Sets out the mechanics of a squeeze and how fixed terms sidestep it.

items.title: GraphTally: How The Graph Solved Micropayments for the Machine Economy
items.tldr: Pay-per-request billing is being treated as new, but The Graph has settled micropayments this way in production since early 2025. Worth reading for the operational lessons rather than the concept.

items.title: Subgraphs or Substreams: Which Blockchain Data Solution Should You Choose?
items.tldr: Subgraphs give structured queryable data for user-facing apps; substreams push high-throughput pipelines. Picks apart which workload each is genuinely built for.

items.title: What "Verifiable" Actually Means for Blockchain Data
items.tldr: Breaks down 1-of-N trust models, consensus and cryptographic verification as separate things, because they get used interchangeably and they guarantee very different amounts.

items.title: 212 Exploits, $1.1B Stolen: Inside Crypto's Bloodiest Half-Year
items.tldr: Blockaid's H1 2026 numbers, including the arrival of prompt injection as a mainstream attack path. Sobering on how much of the loss required no cryptographic break at all.

items.title: AI Agents Can Now Pay on Your Behalf: MoonPay's PayBox Explained
items.tldr: Passkey vaults plus x402 let a chat assistant move real money. Walks through the flow and, more usefully, where the spending limits actually bind.

items.title: Wall Street Just Ran Its First Live Trades on Blockchain
items.tldr: DTCC executed live production trades in tokenised securities with 40+ firms including JPMorgan and Goldman. Notable for being production rather than another pilot.

items.title: Enterprise Custody: Air-Gapped Multi-Signature Signing for Security Tokens
items.tldr: The signing device never connects to a network, and that is the architecture rather than a setting. QR-based air gap, with multi-sig quorum enforced as onchain permissions instead of database rows.

items.title: Transfer Agent Administration: On-Chain Cap Tables
items.tldr: The blockchain ledger becomes the authoritative cap table, so there is nothing to reconcile. ERC-1404 runs five compliance checks before every transfer, and failures revert with a full audit trail.

items.title: Hyperliquid-Powered Stock and Commodity Leveraged Tokens
items.tldr: 2x and 3x tokens on NVDA and the Nasdaq 100, built on perp markets. A concrete look at how leveraged exposure to equities gets wrapped into a single token.

items.title: Inside Toros Bitcoin Short Volatility
items.tldr: Takes a structured product apart into its two components, a covered call position and an actively rebalanced short. Short, and unusually willing to show the construction.

items.title: Leveraged Gold Exposure on Ethereum and Arbitrum
items.tldr: Explains the wider project of turning complex leveraged strategies into one holdable token, and what gets abstracted away when you do that.

items.title: Batched L2 Details: The Explorer Feature You're Probably Missing
items.tldr: Rollups post transactions to L1 in batches, and most explorers hide that layer entirely. Explains what batching does to cost and finality, and why seeing it matters.

items.title: How to Verify Smart Contracts on OP Stack, Step by Step
items.tldr: Verification is what lets anyone read the source behind a deployed address. A straightforward walkthrough for OP Stack chains, where the process differs slightly from mainnet.

items.title: Tracking Every OP Stack L1 to L2 Interaction
items.tldr: Deposits and withdrawals between layers are where rollup users most often lose track of funds. On monitoring that boundary continuously rather than checking after the fact.

items.title: Build Your First SubQuery Project in 10 Minutes
items.tldr: A short hands-on route into blockchain indexing: stand up a working project and query it end to end, which teaches the data model far faster than reading about it.

items.title: Why Newly-Launched Rollups and Appchains Need a Different Indexer
items.tldr: A new rollup has no indexing infrastructure on day one and no history to backfill. Covers what an appchain actually needs from an indexer and how that differs from an established chain.

items.title: AAA and Industry Leaders Launch a Legal Protocol for Agentic Commerce
items.tldr: If an agent enters a contract, someone has to be liable and someone has to arbitrate. An early attempt at the legal scaffolding, which is further along than most people realise.

items.title: The EUDI Wallet, Explained: What It Is and How Businesses Accept It
items.tldr: Europe is standardising a government-backed identity wallet, and acceptance will not be optional for long. Explains the moving parts from the relying party's side.

items.title: ADGM Proposes a Regulatory Framework for Virtual Asset Staking
items.tldr: Abu Dhabi moving to regulate staking matters mostly for what it defines: who is a validator, who is a custodian, and where the liability for slashing lands.

items.title: ETFs, DATs and the New Economics of On-Chain Yield
items.tldr: A data-led look at how ETFs and digital asset treasuries are redirecting capital, and what that does to staking liquidity when large passive holders arrive.

items.title: The Institutional Onchain Rail Is Being Assembled in Public
items.tldr: Tokenised cash management, securities settlement and custody are converging piece by piece. Tracks who is building which part, rather than treating it as one inevitable trend.

items.title: 20+ Skills and MCP Servers for Blockchain Development
items.tldr: A survey of 20+ AI skills and MCP servers that expose blockchain infrastructure to models, and how they change a developer's actual workflow rather than just the demo.

items.title: Introducing Agentic Payments with Turnkey
items.tldr: Production infrastructure for agent payments: non-custodial wallets, gas sponsorship, real-time balances and policy controls. The policy layer is what makes the rest safe to run.

items.title: Turnkey for Agent Identity: ERC-8004 and Trustless AI
items.tldr: The execution and identity layer that has to exist before an agent can be trusted with money, covering ERC-8004 identities and SIWA authentication together.

items.title: Bounty Programs: The First Step in Stopping the Crypto Hack Epidemic
items.tldr: A bounty only works if the payout beats what the exploit is worth, which is a harder economic condition to satisfy than most programmes admit. Honest about that limit.

items.title: Crypto Private Key Theft Is Now Big Business
items.tldr: A short brief on key theft as an organised commercial operation rather than opportunistic crime, and what that shift means for how custody has to be designed.

items.title: Your Crypto's Not as Safe as You Think: How Modern Hackers Hunt Private Keys
items.tldr: Key theft has been industrialised: what once needed a skilled operator now runs as tooling anyone can rent. Long report on how that pipeline actually works end to end.

items.title: Beyond JSON-RPC: How Unified Data Schemas Simplify Multi-Chain Frontends
items.tldr: Building across many chains feels like translating a dozen languages at once. Makes the case for normalising at the schema level rather than in every component.

items.title: Live Smart Routing to the Best Web3 RPC Provider
items.tldr: Providers degrade at different times and in different regions, so the best endpoint is not a fixed choice. On measuring and switching continuously rather than picking once.

items.title: Web3 Infrastructure Health Scorecard: A Deep Dive
items.tldr: Breaks down each pillar and metric used to judge whether infrastructure is actually healthy. Worth reading for the definitions alone, since most uptime claims skip them.

items.title: DualPool Hook: A Technical Deep Dive
items.tldr: A v4 hook that parks idle market-maker inventory in a lending market until the moment a swap needs it. Walks through the accounting and the edge cases that make doing so safe.

items.title: Introducing Permissioned Pools on Uniswap v4
items.tldr: A hook standard for trading assets that carry compliance constraints, with the eligibility checks enforced onchain at swap time rather than bolted on at the interface layer.

items.title: DeFi Yield Strategies: Mechanics, Risk and Returns
items.tldr: Seven strategies account for most of what onchain vaults do, and each earns its return by taking a different risk that the headline APY never reveals. Why yield numbers travel so badly.

items.title: How Companies Earn Yield on Idle Treasury Cash
items.tldr: Six structures compete for the same idle corporate cash and mostly draw on the same short-dated paper, so the rate converges. What separates them is liquidity, minimum size and counterparty.

items.title: From Bank Account to EUR0, No Exchange Needed
items.tldr: Reaching a euro stablecoin normally means an exchange, an intermediate token and several fees. Describes collapsing that path, and what has to be regulated for it to be legal.

items.title: Two Markets. One Spread. One Yield. Zero Direction.
items.tldr: A market-neutral position built from Hyperliquid funding against Aave credit. Worth reading for how the two legs offset, and for what breaks the neutrality when they stop.

items.title: HSM-Based Digital Asset Custody for Banks
items.tldr: A hardware security module protects the key and does nothing about who asked it to sign. On the policy, approval and segregation layers a bank still has to build around it.

items.title: Private Stablecoin Payments for Institutions
items.tldr: Institutions want stablecoin settlement without broadcasting payroll and treasury movements to everyone. Covers how a privacy layer sits under payments while staying governable.

items.title: FiDA, MiCA, and the Future of EU Crypto Data Sharing
items.tldr: Two EU regimes arriving at once, one about markets and one about data access. Explains how they interlock and what had to be in place before the July 2026 MiCA deadline.

items.title: Open Finance Stack: Bank, Investment, and Crypto Data
items.tldr: Connecting a bank, a broker and a wallet means three auth models and three data shapes. Walks the APIs, consent flows and normalisation layer that make them one view.

items.title: Open Finance vs. Open Banking: What's the Real Difference?
items.tldr: Open banking covers accounts and payments; open finance reaches investments, pensions and crypto. The regulatory backing behind each differs sharply, which decides what you can build on.

items.title: Best Practices to Secure Your Assets
items.tldr: Written around setting up a clean machine, which is the right frame: most compromises trace back to the environment rather than the wallet itself.

items.title: Common Trends With Phishing in Web3
items.tldr: Short catalogue of the patterns that recur across Web3 phishing. Dated now, but the underlying tricks have proved remarkably durable.

items.title: Agentic Memory Debt: Why Your Agents Keep Accumulating It
items.tldr: An agent that forgets everything between sessions rebuilds the same context forever, and one that remembers everything drowns. On the compounding cost sitting between those.

items.title: An Open Standard for Agentic Trading
items.tldr: If agents are going to trade, their records need to be verifiable by someone who was not there. Describes what such a standard has to capture to be worth anything after the fact.

items.title: Bringing Walrus to the IPFS Ecosystem Through Lighthouse
items.tldr: Two decentralised storage models with different durability guarantees, bridged without forcing anyone to migrate. Good for understanding what content addressing does and does not promise.

items.title: Gas Sponsorship in Web3: Concepts, Tools, and Implementation
items.tldr: Covers relayers, meta-transactions, smart accounts and ERC-4337 as one connected story rather than four separate buzzwords, which is how they actually fit together.

items.title: How Cross-Chain MEV and Private Order Flow Disrupt Chain Abstraction
items.tldr: Extraction is about positioning and speed, not just trading. Explains why abstracting chains away from the user makes the value being extracted underneath harder to see.

items.title: The Hidden Complexity of Solver Rebalancing in Intent-Based Systems
items.tldr: Solvers have to hold inventory across chains to fill intents, and that inventory drifts. On why rebalancing quietly decides whether an intent system stays fair or efficient.

items.title: Inside DTCC's Tokenization Pilot: TradFi Meets Blockchain
items.tldr: DTCC put live tokenized trades through with BlackRock, JPMorgan and Goldman ahead of its October 2026 launch. Detail on settlement infrastructure being rebuilt rather than displaced.

items.title: What Is a Self-Custody Wallet In Cryptocurrency?
items.tldr: Holding your own keys trades counterparty risk for operational risk. Compares the wallet types and is unusually willing to say when self-custody is the wrong choice.

items.title: Migrating From Standard Relay to Executor Relay
items.tldr: A deprecation guide that doubles as an explanation of how cross-chain message delivery is actually paid for and who is responsible when it stalls.

items.title: The Monad Native Bridge: A User Playbook
items.tldr: Step by step for moving assets to a new chain, which is the moment users most often lose funds by picking the wrong route or the wrong token representation.

items.title: Updates to Wormhole's Supported Networks
items.tldr: Chains get deprecated, and anything bridged to them becomes someone's problem. A useful look at the unglamorous lifecycle question most interoperability writing skips.

items.title: 2025 in Review: The Rise of Casual Degen Gaming
items.tldr: A year of Web3 gaming summarised by someone who had money on the outcome. Useful as a record of what the category actually did rather than what it promised.

items.title: An Explosion of Casual Games, Powered by AI
items.tldr: On what happens to game economies when production costs collapse and the supply of games rises sharply. Relevant well beyond the guild model.

items.title: Institutional DeFi Is Not a Liquidity Problem, It's an Identity Problem
items.tldr: The usual explanation for slow institutional adoption is thin liquidity. This argues the real blocker is that funds cannot prove who they are trading with without doxxing themselves.

items.title: MiCA 2026: CASP Compliance Without Raw Identity Custody
items.tldr: MiCA obliges crypto service providers to know their customers; it does not oblige them to warehouse identity documents. Works through where that distinction actually survives contact with a regulator.

items.title: Proof Over Copies: A Better Way to Verify Identity
items.tldr: Most KYC works by taking a copy of your passport and keeping it, which turns every verifier into a future breach. The alternative proves a fact without surrendering the document.
